plan.designSource: The child's own spec is empty; the plan applies the parent spec dispatch://LEGSMOKE-1009/spec with the key LEGSMOKE-1014 substituted, as every earlier 'Upgrade rehearsal push child' plan did. The architect decides whether to write the child's spec.

commitMessages.reviewRound: smoke: append review line to LEGSMOKE-1014 marker

plan.ciCheck: gh api 'repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/commits/<ciHead>/check-runs?per_page=100' --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name=="gate" or .name=="check")] | {names: (map(.name)|unique), states: (map(.status+"/"+(.conclusion//"pending"))|unique)}' must print {"names":["check","gate"],"states":["completed/success"]}; handoff heads carry skip-checks and are compared to <ciHead> with gh api 'repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/compare/<ciHead>...<head>' --jq '[.files[].filename | startswith(".legion/LEGSMOKE-1014/")] | all' -> true
plan.surface: GitHub via the pane's plain gh (contents, commits, check-runs, pulls/<N>/files, pr diff) at named SHAs; jj in $LEGION_WORKSPACE for local pre-push checks; production is main read at the merge commit

implement: legion-worker: binding to $LEGION_WORKSPACE, the shared-workspace commit rule, the push/trailer rule, the PR body template and proof definition (references/pr-body.md), review-thread resolution (references/review-threads.md), and the production check (references/merge-gate.md).
legion-retro: the implementer is revived for retro and must make the one removal commit of .legion/LEGSMOKE-1014/ (pushed without the trailer) and the Retro Complete Dispatch message.
dispatch: the production check posts one dispatch message on LEGSMOKE-1014; no repository skill exists (no AGENTS.md, docs/, PR template or test harness in sjawhar/legion-smoke).
test: legion-worker: references/pr-body.md defines what the tester verifies (drive the real GitHub surface, judge the implementer's proof, read CI, never rerun it) and the test.json fields (implementerProof, failures, proof); no repository test harness exists, so the tester's commands are the plan's fixed GET-only read list (T4) with literal expected outputs and no test file is added.
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md (required-set read from the ruleset and branch protection, review submission by SHA of the head the handoff push made, round order) and references/review-threads.md (one disposition per thread; an optional one-line append request per the parent spec's Scope); no repository review skill exists.

findings.finding: The child's own spec is empty, so no document in LEGSMOKE-1014 states the file, content or review-append rule; the design traces only to the parent spec plus the planner's inference.
findings.answer: plan.md 'Where the design comes from' and plan.designSource: the parent spec dispatch://LEGSMOKE-1009/spec governs with the key substituted; the completion summary names the empty spec so the architect can decide whether to write it; a child spec that differs re-runs planning (Risks).

findings.finding: 'Both workflows pass on the final head' collides with the phase order if retro's removal push carried skip-checks and ran no workflows.
findings.answer: D5: skill://legion-worker lists retro's removal of .legion/<KEY>/ among pushes that carry no trailer, so the READY head runs both workflows and is its own <ciHead>; CI row and T7.

findings.finding: 'On first push wc -l = 1' is ambiguous because the planner's handoff push precedes any code.
findings.answer: D3: the criterion attaches to <implSha>, the first commit adding smoke/LEGSMOKE-1014.md; AC2 reads the file at ?ref=<implSha>.

findings.finding: The ruleset requires only gate while the spec names both workflows, and each SHA yields duplicate check/gate runs from push and pull_request events.
findings.answer: D4 states CI as a set condition over every check and gate run at <ciHead> ({names:[check,gate], states:[completed/success]}); D6 says the ruleset's single context is necessary, not sufficient.

findings.finding: wc -l counts newlines, so a missing trailing LF reads 0 and a stray blank line reads 2; no document pins the bytes.
findings.answer: D1 pins 44 bytes / sha256 06cd64fa…7307d; AC2 checks sha256sum, --jq .size, tail -c1 | xxd -p -> 0a, not wc -l alone.

findings.finding: Dropping the (/tmp/…) title suffix is an unwritten convention.
findings.answer: D1 cites smoke/LEGSMOKE-1004.md (and every earlier marker) as the source; the acceptance is equality with the pinned constant plus containment of the key.

findings.finding: Line 2's text is unpinned and a no-append review must also pass.
findings.answer: D2 pins 'Legion proof review round 1 (LEGSMOKE)' (24-file precedent) unless the thread names a line; AC3a/AC3b branch on the review's outcome.

findings.finding: docs/solutions/ optional or required is undecided; the repo has no docs/ directory.
findings.answer: D7: permitted, not required (precedent #744 merged the marker alone); AC4b checks the literal sorted file list from pulls/<N>/files.

findings.finding: The changed-files criterion is only satisfiable after retro deletes .legion/LEGSMOKE-1014/; no time point is given.
findings.answer: D8 defines two evaluation points: pre-retro (handoff paths expected) and READY head (none); T7 makes the removal an acceptance item.

findings.finding: The production check assumes a squash merge and does not say how the merge SHA is obtained.
findings.answer: D11/D12: <mergeSha> from gh pr view <N> --json mergeCommit; the commits/<mergeSha> file list is checked whichever strategy GitHub used; T9.

findings.finding: The 'no earlier commit on main' control flips after the merge.
findings.answer: D9 pins the control to commits?sha=cd982c1a…&path=… -> 0 with positive control LEGSMOKE-1004.md -> 1; AC1 names before/after readings separately.

findings.finding: 'Read-only negative controls' is unbounded and invites creating .fail-me.
findings.answer: D9 enumerates GET-only controls and forbids creating .fail-me, scratch files, branches, tags, PR comments or GitHub-issue writes for any proof.

findings.finding: No test harness exists, so 'the tester verifies' has no command to run.
findings.answer: D10 and T4: a fixed list of GitHub reads with literal expected outputs plus six GET-only break attempts; no test file; the reason recorded in test.json.

findings.finding: Who pushes the planner's handoff and when is a hidden sequencing requirement.
findings.answer: D14: the planner commits plan.json and pushes only on the proof driver's targeted message; the implementer's first push carries it beneath the code commit, so it appears in the pre-retro diff (D8a).

findings.finding: Measured facts (main head, branch head, ruleset, .fail-me, skip-checks behaviour) can drift before the implementer acts.
findings.answer: The facts table is dated 2026-10-22T22:55Z; D13 requires the implementer to re-run the reads before the first push and record its own outputs; a moved main licenses no rebase.
